experiment: multi-step rollout loss -> predictor goal-directedness -> GWMR planner re-test
implementation: tiny_jepa/train.py: _rollout_branch (BPTT through H=5 unrolled predictor steps, decay 0.9, opt-in via rollout_steps/rollout_weight); gradient verified vs finite differences (rel err < 0.005)

toward_away_ordering.note: 20 seeds, 6-step imagined toward vs away sequences

drift.note: imagined-vs-true latent L2 at rollout steps 1..6

root_cause: The planner exploits a predictor artifact: action 0 (stay) is ALWAYS chosen because the predictor is most accurate when nothing changes, so the imagined 'stay' latent has lower distance-to-goal than any 'move' latent. CEM converges to [0,0,0,...] every step; the agent never moves. This is a planning-formulation bug, not a model bug: absolute distance-to-goal rewards inaction under model uncertainty. The toward/away probe (0.80) forced movement-vs-movement comparison and showed the predictor IS goal-directed; the planner just never gets to use it because 'stay' dominates. Fix: score PROGRESS (dist(z0,zg) - dist(z_imagined,zg)) instead of absolute distance, so staying still scores 0.
honest_verdict: Rollout training WORKED: ordering 0.60->0.80, drift flattened (3.2->1.8 at step 6). The predictor is now the most goal-directed it has ever been. But the GWMR planner still scores 0.00 because of the stay-exploit formulation bug — a planner-side issue, not a model-side issue. The full day's arc is now complete: encoder OK (wall geometry), metric OK (SIGReg), predictor OK (rollout) — the remaining bug is in how CEM scores. A progress-based score should fix it; that is the single concrete next step.

progress_scoring_experiment.implementation: tiny_jepa/planning_gwmr.py: score_type="progress" (opt-in; "absolute" preserved). Score = -(d0 - d_imagined) so CEM minimizes; staying still scores ~0, moving toward goal scores negative (=positive progress). With score_mode="min", d is min_t d_t so this is max-over-trajectory progress.
progress_scoring_experiment.protocol: 20 episodes x 64 steps, seeds 5000..5019 (same as prior evals)
progress_scoring_experiment.movement_check: YES — agent moves now (43-58% non-stay actions vs ~0% under the original stay-exploit). The stay-exploit formulation bug is fixed.
progress_scoring_experiment.wall_routing: Partial: in 12 episodes needing detours around the horizontal wall, agent went through the right-side gap 5-6 times. But sample trajectories show it then gets stuck bumping walls (e.g. path_len 1-2px over 64 steps despite 27+ move actions) — it approaches walls but cannot convert to pellet capture.
progress_scoring_experiment.deeper_diagnosis: Per-action progress probe (agent at (4.7,18.2), true pellet at (22.5,18.2), directly right): move-right progress = -0.195 (NEGATIVE), move-up = +0.144. The latent progress signal points AWAY from the pellet. Holds even with TRUE pellet position for the goal embedding, so this is not just perception error (perceived pellet was 5-9px off, sometimes inside the wall bar). The encoder separates walls coarsely (3.2x probe) but its fine-grained metric does not decrease monotonically as the agent physically approaches the goal — SIGReg steepened the gradient 2x but did not make it task-aligned.
progress_scoring_experiment.honest_verdict: Progress scoring fixed the stay-exploit (agent moves) but did NOT unlock the planner (0.00-0.05 pellets). The full day’s diagnostic chain now ends at a sharper claim: every component works in isolation (encoder geometry ✓, SIGReg metric ✓, rollout predictor ✓, progress formulation ✓) but the composed system still fails because the latent distance landscape is not task-aligned at planning resolution — it knows about walls but not which direction is "toward the pellet" in latent space. Next frontier would be a task-aligned metric (e.g. successor-feature-style or goal-conditioned value in latent space), not another planner tweak.
